title: Rav Assi bar Natan
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In [Shabbat 53a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.53a.4-6) he asked Rav Chiyya bar Ashi and raised an objection to him; Rabbi Zeira said to him, “Leave him; he holds like his teacher (Rav).” In [Nedarim 78a](https://www.sefaria.org/Nedarim.78a.10) Rav Assi bar Natan came to Nehardea to Rav Sheshet and did not find him; he followed him to Mechoza.
In [Bava Batra 121a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.121a.2) it reads Rabbi Yose bar Natan, whom Hyman identifies as Rav Assi bar Natan.

In [Berakhot 62a](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.62a.10) he disagrees with Ulla, and there it is Issi bar Natan; Hyman reports that Dikdukei Soferim reads: “Rav Assi bar Natan teaches Ulla’s statement thus.”[^3]

notes.text: The supplied מרבב is read as מרב. Saved Davidson Shabbat 53a has Chiyya bar Rav Ashi in the question but Chiyya bar Ashi in Zeira’s supporting quotation. The supplied Nedarim 53a journey has no match in the saved bounded whole-folio text; no work-wide absence is claimed. That source question keeps p001 held.

The earlier note records the search before the journey was located. Hyman’s printed entry (vol. I, pp. 240–241) gives Nedarim 53a. The journey described, from Nehardea to Mechoza in search of Rav Sheshet, is at Nedarim 78a, and the immediate reply continues on 78b. Bava Batra 121a tells the parallel with Rabbi Yosei bar Natan. The equating of the names is Hyman’s interpretation. The consulted Berakhot 62a gives Issi bar Natan teaching a version of Ulla’s statement. The reading from Dikdukei Soferim is reported by Hyman.

Shabbat names Chiyya bar Rav Ashi in Assi’s question, but Chiyya bar Ashi in the teaching Zeira cites in Rav’s name. The response to Assi’s question continues at [Nedarim 78b](https://www.sefaria.org/Nedarim.78b.1). The Bava Batra parallel names Yose bar Natan. The consulted Berakhot gives Issi reciting a variant version of the rule that Ulla states immediately before. Heilprin’s separate [Issi](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=437&lang=en) and [Assi](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=617&lang=en) notices both refer to his Yose notice. Hyman’s equation is an interpretation.
